facts: The petitioners, Kannan Devan Hills Produce Company Ltd., brought a writ petition under art. 32 of the Constitution.
The petitioners are in possession of an area of approximately 1,27,904 acres, commonly known as the 'Concession Area' lying contiguously in the Kannan Devan Hills village.
The petitioners grow and manufacture tea in the plantations set up and developed by them.
The petitioners' predecessor-in-title was one Mr. John Danial Munro, who obtained a concession from Punhatil Kayikal Kela Varma Valuja Raja on July 11, 1877.

A Royal Proclamation was made on September 24, 1899, declaring the tract known as Anjanad and Kannan Devan Hills an integral portion of the territory and all rights over it belong to and vest in the State.

The petitioners have established 23 tea estates with factories for the manufacture of tea, hospitals, quarters, and township, and are employing approximately 18,500 persons for the running of the said estates.
issues: Whether the Kannan Devan Hills (Resumption of Lands) Act, 1971 is within the legislative competence of the State of Kerala?
Whether the impugned Act is protected from challenge under art. 31A of the Constitution?
petitioner_arguments: The petitioners have been holding, cultivating, enjoying and dealing with the Concession Land as the absolute owner thereof.

The petitioners have established 23 tea estates with factories for the manufacture of tea, hospitals, quarters, and township, and are employing approximately 18,500 persons for the running of the said estates.
court_reasoning: The court held that the impugned Act is within the legislative competence of the State of Kerala.
The court also held that the impugned Act is protected from challenge under art. 31A of the Constitution.
holding: The Supreme Court upheld the validity of the Kannan Devan Hills (Resumption of Lands) Act, 1971 and dismissed the petition.
